title: Preservation and Progress of the Search Invariant
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and $S$ a bit string. Suppose there are natural numbers $c,d$ and a bit $b$ such that $S=\langle\operatorname{bits}(c),\langle\operatorname{bits}(d),[b]\rangle\rangle$, where $2^{\lceil\log_2(2n)\rceil}<c\leq q$, $2\leq d\leq c$, no integer $m$ with $2\leq m<d$ divides $c$, and $b$ can be true only when $c=q$; here $q$ is the least prime greater than $2^{\lceil\log_2(2n)\rceil}$. Then one search step preserves these conditions. It strictly decreases the specified search measure whenever that measure is positive, and leaves $S$ unchanged whenever that measure is zero.
hypotheses_covered: S is a bit string satisfying the full stated search invariant
The strict-decrease conclusion assumes the search measure is positive
The unchanged-state conclusion assumes the search measure is zero
